Canonical destination is https://campaign-site-azure.vercel.app/. The 2026-09-06 entry above named teams.doviloop.dev; that subdomain was never stood up as the campaign page. It resolves, answers, and 301s to https://www.doviloop.dev/ - the product home page. The price half of the 2026-09-06 decision is untouched and still stands.
_decisions.evidence: curl -sIL https://teams.doviloop.dev/ -> HTTP/2 301, location: http://doviloop.dev -> 308 -> https://www.doviloop.dev/ 200. Measured 2026-09-14. https://campaign-site-azure.vercel.app/?utm_... returns 200 with the query string intact, so attribution survives the landing.
_decisions.why_it_mattered: An ad pointed at teams.doviloop.dev would have looked healthy - 200 at the end of the chain - while sending every paid click to a page with no qualifier, no lead form and none of this campaign's instrumentation. Six creative destinations, creative/hours.json, creative/capacity.json, the Ads Manager paste sheet in campaigns/structure.md and two audience definitions all carried it. A test asserted it.
_decisions.reversible: Yes. If the subdomain is repointed at the campaign site, change ORIGIN in tests/test_copy.py and the six destination fields.

_decisions.decision: Canonical destination is https://teams.doviloop.dev/ again. The 2026-09-14 entry above named the .vercel.app deployment URL, correctly, because the subdomain did 301 to the product site when it was written. It no longer does.
_decisions.evidence: teams.doviloop.dev was a Porkbun URL Forward reached through a WILDCARD - *.doviloop.dev CNAME pixie.porkbun.com - not a record of its own; a hostname nobody had ever created 301'd identically. Adding a specific `teams` CNAME to Vercel's per-project target beat the wildcard without deleting it. Measured after cutover: / , /da and /lt all 200 with zero redirects, title 'DoviLoop for teams', certificate issued for teams.doviloop.dev itself.
_decisions.why_it_mattered: The .vercel.app host cannot be verified in Business Manager - vercel.app is on the Public Suffix List and Meta verifies at eTLD+1 - so an ad pointed there could never have Aggregated Event Measurement. It also reads as a staging URL in the ad.

attestations._note: Attestations for numbers - digits AND number words: one, half, twice, dozen - appearing in a spoken ad field. Keyed by sha256('<field>.<lang>' + '|' + spoken text), where spoken text has ** stripped and whitespace collapsed; engine.gate.evidence_key('headline.en', text) computes it and a failing gate prints the exact key to add. kind is one of: measured (has a stopwatch or a dataset behind it), architectural (true by construction of the code), illustrative (a rhetorical cardinal in narrator prose, not a quantitative claim). Same policy, same hashing as reel-engine/claims/evidence.json, so a hook attested there is attested here for the same field name. Empty on purpose: no ad has yet needed a number.
